extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, journalism students, and news organizations
extracted.subtask_description: A statement of broad ethical principles and actionable guidance for journalists and media professionals about accuracy, minimizing harm, independence, and accountability in reporting across all media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — purpose of the code
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. Ethical journalism strives to ensure the free exchange of information that is accurate, fair and thorough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code declares four principles as the foundation of ethical journalism and encourages their use by all people in all media. It is a guide to encourage responsibility for information provided; it should be read as a whole and not as legally enforceable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism should be accurate and fair. Journalists should be honest and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This foundational principle covers verification, sourcing, context, avoiding distortion, and giving voice to the voiceless. See the specific 'Journalists should' items for concrete behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take responsibility for the accuracy of their work
rubrics_metrics.description: Take responsibility for the accuracy of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify information before releasing it. Use original sources whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neither speed nor format excuses inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that neither speed nor format excuses inaccuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain verification standards regardless of deadlines or distribution platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and avoid misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context. Take special care not to misrepresent or oversimplify in promoting, previewing or summarizing a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure headlines, teasers, and summaries accurately reflect story nuance and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather, update and correct throughout a story's life
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather, update and correct information throughout the life of a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reporting as an ongoing process; publish updates and corrections as new information emerges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with promises and keep promised commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious when making promises, but keep the promises they make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overpromising confidentiality or outcomes; honor commitments to sources when ethically appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public is entitled to as much information as possible to judge the reliability and motivations of sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider motives before granting anonymity; explain anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider sources’ motives before promising anonymity. Reserve anonymity for sources who may face danger, retribution or other harm, and have information that cannot be obtained elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why anonymity was granted so audiences can assess credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligently seek subjects to allow response
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek subjects of news coverage to allow them to respond to criticism or allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give people fair opportunity to comment before publication when practical and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undercover or surreptitious methods unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information unless traditional, open methods will not yield information vital to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secret methods only when the public interest clearly outweighs the intrusion and when open methods have been exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold power accountable; give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable. Give voice to the voiceless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that scrutinizes institutions and amplifies underrepresented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open and civil exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open and civil exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate public discourse while maintaining civility and allowing diverse opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as watchdogs over public affairs and government
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to serve as watchdogs over public affairs and government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek to ensure that the public’s business is conducted in the open, and that public records are open to all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to source material when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to source material when it is relevant and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share documents, recordings, and evidence that help audiences evaluate reporting, while balancing privacy and safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse human experiences; seek seldom-heard voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Boldly tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek sources whose voices we seldom hear to broaden coverage and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping; examine personal biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should examine the ways their values and experiences may shape their reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label advocacy and commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Label advocacy and commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish opinion/advocacy from news reporting so audiences are not misled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never deliberately distort facts or context
rubrics_metrics.description: Never deliberately distort facts or context, including visual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label illustrations and re-enactments to avoid misleading audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize; always attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always provide attribution for others' work and acknowledge sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism treats sources, subjects, colleagues and members of the public as human beings deserving of respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle covers balancing public interest with privacy, showing compassion, special care for vulnerable people, and considering long-term effects of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance public's need for information against potential harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the public’s need for information against potential harm or discomfort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance or undue intrusiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion and use heightened sensitivity for vulnerable subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected by news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use heightened sensitivity when dealing with juveniles, victims of sex crimes, and sources or subjects who are inexperienced or unable to give consent. Consider cultural differences in approach and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal access is not always ethical justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that legal access to information differs from an ethical justification to publish or broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Just because information can be obtained legally does not mean it should be published without weighing ethical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private people have greater right to control information
rubrics_metrics.description: Realize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than public figures and others who seek power, influence or attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the consequences of publishing or broadcasting personal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity, even if others do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist sensationalism that exploits victims or appeals to prurient interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance suspect's fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a suspect’s right to a fair trial with the public’s right to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the implications of identifying criminal suspects before they face legal charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-term implications and permanence of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the long-term implications of the extended reach and permanence of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide updated and more complete information as appropriate and be mindful of enduring impacts on people’s lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest and primary obligation of ethical journalism is to serve the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle emphasizes avoiding conflicts of interest, refusing improper gifts, and maintaining independence from advertisers and special interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest; disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose unavoidable conflicts so audiences can judge potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid political and other outside activities that may compromise integrity or impartiality, or may damage credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay for access; identify paid content or outside-provided content
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; do not pay for access to news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify content provided by outside sources, whether paid or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers, donors, or special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers, donors or any other special interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist internal and external pressure to influence coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising; label sponsored content
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominently label sponsored content to preserve audience trust and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable and Transparent (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalism means taking responsibility for one’s work and explaining one’s decisions to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle focuses on explaining decisions, responding to concerns, correcting errors, and exposing unethical conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain ethical choices and encourage civil dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain ethical choices and processes to audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage a civil dialogue with the public about journalistic practices, coverage and news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond quickly to questions about accuracy, clarity and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be accessible and timely when audiences raise concerns or seek clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge mistakes and correct them promptly and prominently
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge mistakes and correct them promptly and prominently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain corrections and clarifications carefully and clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical conduct in journalism, including internally
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical conduct in journalism, including within their organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold peers and institutions to the same standards; do not hide unethical behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by the same high standards expected of others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards they expect of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should model the ethical behavior they demand from subjects and peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code is a guide, not legally enforceable rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics is a statement of abiding principles supported by explanations and position papers. It is not a set of rules, rather a guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code should be read as a whole; individual principles should not be taken out of context. It is not legally enforceable under the First Amendment.
